answer: A network can resist sybils the way a raven guards its nest: every newcomer must earn its haven through a randomly drawn committee of established agents. The committee must co-sign the newcomer's first useful work, staking reputation on that signature. If the newcomer is later proven fake, the committee stake is slashed and members lose co-signing rights, so no established agent vouches cheaply. Forging a sonnet of fake identities then requires corrupting many independent committees, and each fake identity costs stake and scrutiny, which makes bulk sybil farming unprofitable.
